annotationRationale: Divisibility is determined by the number of factors of 2. The complementary event has two disjoint forms, whose probabilities follow from independence. The reviewed equivalent AMC 10B method applies unchanged.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Failure means the product contains zero or one factor of 2. Its probability is (1/2)^6+6(1/3)(1/2)^5=5/64, giving 59/64, choice C. The statement, choices and key agree; no figures are needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2021_Fall_AMC_10B_Q14 / count-missing-factors-of-two is retained and independently verified for this question. The supplemental comparison resolves the earlier choicesMatch flag: all five choices agree mathematically. LIVE and AoPS supply the same complementary-event route, so another method is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Prime exponents, complementary events and independence are appropriate assessed concepts. Classical probability and addition of disjoint probabilities appropriately support the calculation.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The two failure cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Their probabilities are 1/64 and 1/16; the factor 6 correctly selects the unique even die. Every remaining outcome supplies at least two factors of 2, so the final probability is 59/64.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question and method are credited. Both inherited references, live-reference-2021_Fall_AMC_10B_Q14 and aops-reference-2021_Fall_AMC_10B_Q14, remain in sourceRefIds alongside the shared-method citation and current-question references. Reuse of the project explanation is transparent; source-informed-original correctly distinguishes it from an official MAA argument.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why counting failures is simpler. Face classifications, independence, the six placements and exhaustiveness are all explained sufficiently for an AMC 12 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five IDs match actual steps: prime-exponent divisibility, finite face probabilities, independence, disjoint addition and complementation.
